AMGN.rationale: AMGN shows genuine operating improvement with Q1 2026 margin expansion (gross margin +450bp YoY to 68.1%, operating margin from 14.5% to 31.0%) and accelerating cash flow (+57.4% YoY OCF). The franchise is diversified across oncology, inflammation, osteoporosis, cardiovascular, and biosimilars, with multiple growth pillars offsetting legacy declines (Enbrel down 37% YoY). However, the balance sheet is extremely leveraged (D/E 6.24x, $57.32B debt vs $9.19B equity), creating structural vulnerability. Valuation is mixed: PE has compressed from ~38x to 27x, but earnings yield of 3.7% sits below the 10Y Treasury yield of 4.68% — unfavorable for a highly indebted issuer. The stock is near 52-week highs ($387.64 vs $398.00), limiting near-term upside. Q2 2026 earnings (released 2026-07-30) showed a beat-and-raise, but per advisory guidance this post-decision-date data cannot be relied upon. Tavneos FDA withdrawal risk ($459M revenue, $2.4B intangible exposure) and MariTide obesity pipeline uncertainty (Phase 2 data not clearly differentiated vs Lilly/Novo) are manageable but real headwinds. Net-net: improving trajectory and solid franchise quality, but balance-sheet risk and yield-vs-rate headwinds cap the score at mildly attractive.
